who: Playford V. Thorson, historian at the University of North Dakota, doctorate in history completed in 1972.

evidence.says: UND's record of Erik Luther Williamson's 1991 study names Dr. Playford V. Thorson as first advisor.
Thorson taught history at UND from 1960, completed his doctorate in 1972, retired in 1995, and co-edited Plains Folk: An Ethnic History of North Dakota.
The authority heading is Thorson, Playford V.; its supporting citation is Plains folk, with Playford V. Thorson named on the title page.

notes: Advisor name, institution and co-edited work connect the supervisor to the authority. UND classifies Williamson's degree as Doctor of Arts, not PhD.

who: Historian of medicine, University of Wisconsin–Madison 1964–71, subsequently Bonn; medical doctorate Basel 1951.

who: Susan S. Silbey, MIT professor of sociology and anthropology specializing in law and organizations; PhD Chicago 1978.

evidence.says: MIT names Susan Silbey as advisor of Hilary Robinson and Anna Wexler, both awarded their degrees in 2017, with the listed dissertation subjects.
MIT reports that Silbey received her Chicago PhD in 1978 and joined MIT in 2001 as professor of sociology and anthropology.
Silbey's MIT publication list includes her 1979 report What the Lower Courts Do.
The heading Silbey, Susan S. is supported by her 1979 work What the lower courts do.

notes: Direct advisor evidence and the identical work in her MIT bibliography and LC record establish the match.

who: Historian of modern Germany at York University from 1989; doctorate Ludwig Maximilian University, Munich.

York reports that Steinisch began teaching there in 1989 and studies German labour history and comparisons with the United States.

The library catalogue identifies Feldman and Steinisch as authors of Industrie und Gewerkschaften 1918–1924, a study of industry and unions in Weimar Germany.

notes: The distinctive name, Munich doctorate, York career and German labour-history publications agree.
